alternatives: The intersection of the strict relations across admissible rules is empty over the complete universe.
A common core exists but does not exceed the count-matched random-rule control.
An exhaustivity, simplicity-selection, invariance, matching or negative control fails.

analysis.comparisonPlan: Classify invariant_under_rule_family only when the admissible-family common core is nonempty, exceeds the random-family common core, and every control passes. Classify complete_convention_dependence when the admissible common-core total is zero. Classify unknown otherwise or after any control failure. Exact equality counts and selected-rule outside-core counts are descriptive locked observables, not alternative thresholds.
analysis.stoppingRule: Apply exactly the five declared deterministic rules and one count-matched random family to every graph in the complete universe. Never add, remove or reorder a rule after results. Permit one deterministic reconstruction only for byte comparison.

controls.purpose: Require the rule selected before results to equal all_maximal under the locked simplicity tuple.
Require every deterministic rule's strict-pair count to survive the fixed relabelling.
Require every random rule to select exactly as many maximal contexts as its deterministic mate.
Require empty and complete graphs to have no family-derived strict relation.

protocol.hypothesis: A nonempty strict-implication core persists across the complete preregistered family of simple invariant context-selection rules and exceeds the core produced by count-matched random rule families.

configuration.randomMatching: for every graph and admissible rule, uniformly shuffle all maximal contexts and select exactly the deterministic rule's context count
requiredInvariances: equivalent score ties include every tied context
simplicityOrder: no label or random seed in deterministic rule
lexicographic rule id as final tie-break
